summary: This area is genuinely strong on the things it was hardened for: every HDF5 export publishes through a temp file + rename(2) so a cancelled or failed write never leaves a partial bundle (BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:349-396); the burned caption wraps instead of truncating and the figure grows to hold it (ResultExport.swift:1747-1762), with a matching `.usesFontLeading` measurement; the PNG metadata record deliberately omits NaN/inf display ranges so one degenerate value cannot drop the whole record (ResultExport.swift:246-253); `exportedImageProvenanceRecord` correctly refuses to stamp origin-fit keys onto products no origin was involved in (ResultExport.swift:262-269); the scientific bundle carries the `strain_weighting` DEVIATION outward rather than leaving it in a comment (ResultExport.swift:479-486); `scientificBundleOmissions` means a partial bundle never reads as a complete one; and `copySidecarFile`/`adoptSessionSidecar` do same-file detection by filesystem identity rather than path string, with honest split status lines on partial failure. The PNG colormap path is byte-compatible with the Metal shader's masked-pixel gray and windowing. The defects below are all in the *figure* half — what the exported pixels claim about themselves. The most serious is that `restoredResultPixelInfo` is written but never cleared, so after any saved result is viewed, every subsequent export carries the old result's pixel size, units and provenance dictionary; the burned scale bar, the burned caption, the PNG metadata and the sidecar rewrite are all downstream of it. The rest are figure-level: the exported colorbar ignores gamma while the image and the on-screen colorbar apply it, a fabricated "1/nm" unit label, and no legend for masked pixels.

findings.title: restoredResultPixelInfo is never cleared, so exports carry a previous result's pixel size, units and provenance
findings.why: `currentResultPersistenceMetadata` reads `restoredResultPixelInfo ?? navigationResultPixelInfo ?? currentScalarPersistenceMetadata` (ResultExport.swift:1699-1701). Its sibling `restoredResultInfo` (kind/displayName/valueUnits) IS cleared at 15 publication sites (AppState.swift:789, 3009, 3469, 3548, 3630, 3659, 3734, 3938, 3984, 4379, 4741, 4939, 4970, 5281 and 2562), and `navigationResultPixelInfo` is cleared in the `didSet` of both `resultImage` and `resultRGBA` (AppState.swift:241-243, 249-251). `restoredResultPixelInfo` is cleared NOWHERE: the only references in the whole tree are its declaration (AppState.swift:263), two assignments on restore (AppState.swift:2950, 2962), two on `selectSavedSessionResult` (ResultExport.swift:840, 852), and three reads (ResultExport.swift:723, 959, 1699). Its own doc comment at AppState.swift:261 claims "New scientific results clear it at publication" — true for `restoredResultInfo`, false for this field, so the comment actively hides the bug. Because it takes precedence, the *names* on an exported figure come from the new product while the *pixel size, pixel units and the entire provenance dictionary* come from the stale one. It is not cleared in `activate` either (AppState.swift:2556-2566 clears `restoredResultInfo` but not this), so it also leaks across datasets. Blast radius: the burned scale bar (ResultExport.swift:207-211), the burned caption via `displayedProduct.sampling`/`.provenance` (AppState.swift:722-726), the PNG metadata keys `pixel_size_row`/`pixel_size_column`/`pixel_units`/`provenance` (ResultExport.swift:242-244, 236), `displayedProduct.quantitativeStatus` (AppState.swift:683-685, since ResultExport.swift:1705 only fills `quantitative_status` when absent and the stale dict supplies it), the on-screen scale bar (AppState.swift:660 → StemImageView.swift:379-388), and `saveCurrentResultToSessionSidecar`, which persists the stale row/column/units/provenance into the sidecar HDF5 for a brand-new result (ResultExport.swift:726-735, reached via the else branch at 725 which calls `currentResultPersistenceMetadata`). ExportProvenanceTests.swift:104-131 exercises only a fresh session with no prior restore, so the suite is green and blind to this.
findings.failureScenario: Open a dataset whose sidecar holds a saved ptychography object phase (pixelSizeRow/Column 0.2, units "A", provenance {source_product: ptychography_object_phase, engine: singleslice, iterations: 40, quantitative_status: quantitative}). `restoreSessionResult` (AppState.swift:2944-2953) sets both `restoredResultInfo` and `restoredResultPixelInfo`. The user then runs a virtual detector: `runVirtualDetector` sets `restoredResultInfo = nil` (AppState.swift:3469) but leaves `restoredResultPixelInfo`. Scan sampling is, say, 15 A/px. File ▸ Export Result Image… now writes a PNG titled "Virtual detector · Circular" whose burned-in scale bar is computed with 0.2 A/px instead of 15 A/px — a bar 75x too short, unrecoverably burned into the pixels — whose burned caption reads "scan space · quantitative · 0.2 A/px · source_product=ptychography_object_phase", and whose JSON Description chunk carries pixel_size_row 0.2, pixel_units "A" and the ptychography provenance dictionary. Pressing "Save to Session" then writes that same wrong sampling and wrong provenance into the sidecar's RealSlice for the virtual image, so a reopen and any later scientific-bundle export inherit it.

findings.title: Exported figure's colorbar ignores gamma, so colors do not map to the printed endpoints
findings.why: `applyColormap` maps a data fraction f to LUT index round(255 * f^(1/gamma)) (ResultExport.swift:1848-1849, matching Colormaps.metal:62-63). The colorbar drawn into the publication figure fills 256 strips with `lut[index]` linearly against height (ResultExport.swift:1806-1813) and labels the ends with `range.high`/`range.low` (1819-1826). So the colorbar strip at height fraction p shows lut[255p], which the image assigns to data fraction p^gamma, not p. The on-screen legend gets this right — `ScalarColorbarView` applies `pow(fraction, 1/max(gamma,0.05))` before indexing the LUT (ScaleBarView.swift:119-121) and is passed `app.displayedResultGamma` (StemImageView.swift:453). The export path passes no gamma at all: `publicationFigure` has no gamma parameter (ResultExport.swift:1740-1745). The record also does not carry gamma — `exportedImageProvenanceRecord` (ResultExport.swift:232-269) stores display_range_low/high but never `resultGamma` or the colormap name, so a reader cannot reconstruct the mapping either. `resultGamma` is a live user control (DatasetInspector.swift:221).
findings.failureScenario: A user displays a DPC magnitude map with range 0–4 mrad and drags Gamma to 0.5 to bring out weak contrast, then exports the PNG. A pixel drawn at the LUT midpoint corresponds to data fraction 0.5^0.5 = 0.707, i.e. 2.83 mrad, but the exported colorbar puts that same color at its own midpoint between the printed 0 and 4, so the reader measures 2.0 mrad — a 40% error read straight off a figure that carries no gamma key to warn them, and which disagrees with the app's own on-screen legend for the identical view.

findings.title: Exporting while the ACOM region selector is active fuses three different products into one figure
findings.why: `showsACOMRegionReference` (AppState.swift:601-607) redirects `displayedResultImage` to `scanNavigationImage` and `displayedProduct` to a synthetic `acom_region_reference` product (AppState.swift:610-611, 666-679), but leaves `resultImage`/`resultRGBA` holding the retained ACOM result. `exportResultImage` mixes the two frames: the pixels come from `resultRGBA`/`resultImage` (ResultExport.swift:183-190), the title from `currentResultDisplayName` (the ACOM name, 213), the PNG metadata from `currentResultPersistenceMetadata` (the ACOM provenance, 236-244), but the caption from `displayedProduct` (the region-reference product, 272-283 — so it reads "scan space · relative" with none of the ACOM keys) and the colorbar endpoints from `resultDisplayedValueRange`, which is computed from `displayedResultImage` = the navigation image, with `displayedResultColormap` = .viridis and range 0..1 (AppState.swift:1094-1121, 632-641). The menu item is enabled purely on `resultImage == nil && resultRGBA == nil` with no workspace-area guard (mac4DSTEMApp.swift:57-59), so Cmd-Shift-E fires while the Map area shows the region reference. Worse for the RGBA case: an IPF·Z map has `resultImage == nil`, which normally makes `resultDisplayedValueRange` nil and suppresses the colorbar (that is the invariant StemImageView.swift:398-408 documents), but `displayedResultImage` is non-nil here, so a numeric viridis colorbar is drawn beside a categorical IPF figure — exactly the "fabricated legend" that `promoteIPFZDisplayIfDefault` (AppState.swift:5250-5255) refuses to create on screen.
findings.failureScenario: Run a full-scan ACOM map, leave IPF·Z displayed, then switch scope to Selected region and start positioning the box (workspaceArea == .map). Press Cmd-Shift-E. The PNG contains the IPF·Z orientation colors, is titled "ACOM full scan · IPF Z", carries ACOM provenance in its Description chunk — and is captioned "scan space · relative · 15 A/px" with no ACOM keys, beside a viridis colorbar labelled with the min and max intensity of the virtual-detector navigation image. The burned caption and the machine-readable metadata describe two different products, and the legend describes a third.

findings.title: CBED export invents the unit "1/nm" when the file supplies a Q scale with no units, and carries no metadata at all
findings.why: `unitLabel: qSize != nil ? (calibration.qPixelUnits ?? "1/nm") : "px"` burns a physical unit the file never supplied. `qPixelSize` and `qPixelUnits` are independent optionals (Calibration.swift:480-481) and `DM4Reader.extractCalibration` sets them independently, with `units(i)` returning nil for an empty Units tag (DM4Reader.swift:466-472); `applySessionCalibration` also sets size and units under separate `if let`s (AppState.swift:2886-2890). The rest of the app is explicitly honest about this state — the readiness report prints "Reciprocal scale lacks supported physical units (no units)" (Calibration.swift:325-329) and the datacube writer falls back to the literal string "pixels" (BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:1439-1440). Only the scale-bar label invents a physical unit. Compounding it, the CBED path never builds a publication figure and calls `savePNG` with no `properties` (ResultExport.swift:617), so the exported pattern carries no title, no caption, no scan position, no log/gamma/contrast state, no source file and no calibration provenance — nothing that could later correct the fabricated label. (The same `?? "1/nm"` exists on screen at DiffractionView.swift:173, but there it is transient; here it is burned into a distributed file.)
findings.failureScenario: A DM4 acquired on a microscope whose Dimension.0 Units tag is written empty but whose Scale is 0.021 (in 1/A) is opened. Export Diffraction Pattern… burns a bar reading "1 1/nm" onto a span that is actually 1 1/A. The exported PNG asserts a reciprocal scale wrong by a factor of 10, it is the only claim the file makes about itself, and there is no metadata chunk in which the absence of units could be recorded.

findings.title: Result figure's scale bar is drawn at physical scale but labelled "px" when the units string is missing
findings.why: `unitLabel: sampling != nil ? (pixel.units ?? "px") : "px"` — both branches yield "px" when units are nil, but `burnScaleBar` is still handed `unitsPerDataPixel: sampling`, the physical size (ResultExport.swift:209-210). `burnScaleBar` then picks a 1-2-5 value in physical units and labels it "px" (ResultExport.swift:1885-1893). Same reachable state as the finding above: `rPixelSize` non-nil with `rPixelUnits` nil, from a DM4 with an empty Dimension.2 Units tag (DM4Reader.swift:468-473) or a sidecar carrying rSize without rUnits (AppState.swift:2881-2885). Unlike the CBED case the number is not fabricated, but the label contradicts the length, and a reader has no way to detect it because the caption repeats the same fallback (ResultExport.swift:278).
findings.failureScenario: A DM4 with real-space Scale 0.5 and an empty Units tag is opened and a virtual detector image exported. The bar spans 40 data pixels and is labelled "20 px". A reader measuring feature sizes off the figure counts 20 pixels where the image contains 40, halving every length they derive — and the PNG metadata records `pixel_size_row: 0.5` with no `pixel_units` key at all (ResultExport.swift:242-244), so the two halves of the file disagree without saying so.

findings.title: After a quarter turn the burned caption's pixel size names a different axis than the burned scale bar
findings.why: The scale bar is correctly orientation-aware: `sampling = orientation.swapsAxes ? (pixel.row ?? pixel.column) : (pixel.column ?? pixel.row)` (ResultExport.swift:207-208), matching the on-screen bar (StemImageView.swift:380-382). `publicationCaption` is not: it unconditionally prints `product.sampling.column ?? product.sampling.row` (ResultExport.swift:277-279). For anisotropic sampling the two numbers differ, and both are burned into the same figure with no axis named. Anisotropic row/column sampling is real for scan-domain products — the physical iDPC branch returns `(rowSamplingAngstrom, columnSamplingAngstrom)` (ResultExport.swift:1471-1473) — and scan-domain products are exactly the ones for which `effectiveRealSpaceDisplayOrientation` can be a quarter turn (AppState.swift:921-923). The caption does append `display_rotation_deg` (ResultExport.swift:293-299), which is what makes the contradiction diagnosable, but only to a reader who already suspects it.
findings.failureScenario: An iDPC projected-phase map on a scan with 0.4 A row sampling and 0.8 A column sampling, displayed rotated 90 deg, is exported. The scale bar is drawn with 0.4 A/px (correct for the rotated horizontal axis) while the caption below it reads "0.8 A/px · display_rotation_deg=90". A reader takes the caption's number, which is the one printed as text, and every distance measured against the bar comes out 2x wrong.

findings.title: Exported strain figures show masked no-fit pixels as gray with no legend, while the app's own screen legend explains them
findings.why: `applyColormap` renders the invalid sentinel as neutral gray (82,82,87) (ResultExport.swift:1843-1846), matching the shader (Colormaps.metal:57-59), and `scientificBundleMaps` masks unindexed strain positions to NaN (ResultExport.swift:501-503) which normalize to that sentinel (DiffractionPattern.swift:37-45). On screen this is explained: `ScalarColorbarView` draws a "gray = masked, no fit" swatch when `displayedResultHasMaskedPixels()` (ScaleBarView.swift:157, StemImageView.swift:455). The publication figure's colorbar draws only the ramp, two `%.4g` numbers and the units string (ResultExport.swift:1801-1834) with no masked swatch, and `publicationCaption` (ResultExport.swift:272-301) says nothing about validity — it carries `basis_mode`, `reference_mode`, `strain_frame`, but not `indexed_fraction`, which IS available in the strain provenance dict (ResultExport.swift:1548). So the app's flagship quantitative product exports without the one piece of information the repo's own priority (1) names: validity. `exportedImageProvenanceRecord` does carry the full provenance dict (ResultExport.swift:236), so the machine-readable half is fine; it is the pixels-plus-legend half — the part that gets pasted into a paper — that omits it.
findings.failureScenario: A strain e_xx map on a partially amorphous region indexes 60% of positions. The exported PNG shows a diverging RdBu field with large dark-gray patches and a colorbar reading -0.02 to 0.02 "strain". A colleague reading the figure has no legend entry for gray and reads it as an out-of-range or near-zero region rather than "no lattice fit here"; nothing in the burned caption says 40% of the field is not a measurement.

findings.title: Bragg-peak CSV exports raw uncalibrated detector coordinates under bare column names
findings.why: `exportBraggPeaksCSV` writes `braggVectors` verbatim (ResultExport.swift:629-637). `braggVectors` is the RAW detection output — every consumer in the app first passes it through `calibratedBraggVectors`, which subtracts the reference origin and applies the elliptical correction (AppState.swift:4753-4777, and e.g. `showBraggMap` at AppState.swift:4743-4744). So the Bragg map the user is looking at when they press Export is in a different frame from the CSV they get. The file has one header line, `scan_x,scan_y,detector_x,detector_y,intensity`, and carries no units, no q pixel size, no origin, no ellipse parameters, no statement that the coordinates are un-recentred, and no source-file or view provenance — unlike the sibling EMD export at ResultExport.swift:648-693, which ships the full `PixelCalibration` alongside so py4DSTEM can apply it. The inline comment at ResultExport.swift:627-628 says only "CSV stays in the app's Cartesian convention", which names the axis convention and is silent about the calibration state, so a reader of the source is not warned either.
findings.failureScenario: A user detects disks on a dataset whose beam centre sits at (61.4, 66.9) rather than the detector middle, exports the CSV, and computes |g| for the innermost ring in a script. Because detector_x/detector_y are un-recentred, every |g| is offset by the origin displacement — several pixels on a 144x144 detector — and the derived lattice spacing is wrong, with nothing in the file to reveal that the origin was never subtracted or that the ellipse correction the app applies internally is missing.
